title: Amp Code: Next Generation AI Coding – Beyang Liu, Amp Code
talk_summary: Beyang Liu describes Amp's opinionated architecture: a small set of custom tools instead of MCP sprawl, specialized sub-agents (finder, oracle, librarian, kraken) to conserve main-context and offload reasoning, and two top-level agents (smart/rush) instead of a user-facing model selector. He also argues review is now the human bottleneck and built a guided diff-review UI with a 'tour of the change'.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of generic sub-agents with tweaked prompts, they ship a few purpose-built ones: a 'finder' (small fast model + limited search toolset) for codebase discovery, a 'librarian' for dependency/framework docs, and a 'kraken' that writes code-mods for large refactors rather than editing files one by one.
takeaways.evidence_quote: sub agents are effectively a way to conserve and extend the context window of your main agent

takeaways.technique: Reasoning as an on-demand sub-agent, not a model selector
takeaways.what_they_do: Rather than exposing a model picker, they keep the main agent snappy and drop into an 'oracle' sub-agent (a deep-reasoning model) only when a problem is tricky or needs planning.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the best way to implement reasoning models is really through a sub agent ... preserve the relative like snappiness uh in the main agent
takeaways.numbers: claims ~4 out of 5 times the oracle finds the underlying issue

takeaways.technique: Curated core toolset over MCP sprawl
takeaways.what_they_do: They deliberately under-invest in MCP integrations and tune a small custom toolset, because MCP authors can't tune descriptions to your agent's loops and extra tools cause context confusion.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the more tools that you add into the context window ... if the tools aren't relevant to the task at hand, it ends up getting confused

takeaways.technique: Guided diff review with a 'tour of the change'
takeaways.what_they_do: They built a custom diff viewer that lets you pick a commit range, view file-level diffs, and gives a guided tour of which files to read first, because review is now the bottleneck.
takeaways.evidence_quote: half the battle when reviewing a large change is figuring out where to start

takeaways.technique: Two top-level agents by modality (smart vs rush)
takeaways.what_they_do: They expose exactly two agents tuned to two work modalities: 'smart' for async complex tasks with sub-agents, 'rush' for tight in-the-loop quick edits, rather than N models x one harness.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're trying to kind of like pick points along the frontier of intelligence and speed that are meaningful to the user experience

takeaways.technique: Shared agent threads for skill transfer
takeaways.what_they_do: They let teammates share agent threads and inspect how others prompt, so prompting techniques propagate across the team.
